newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico business chief wants deregulation, rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Mexico business chief wants deregulation, rate cut.

text.p: The head of the influential Mexican Employers Confederation (Coparmex) called on the government to cut interest rates, deregulate, simplify the tax system and revamp social policy.
In interviews with Mexican newspapers ahead of the Coparmex National Assembly, which begins this morning in the northern state of Baja California, Coparmex president Carlos Abascal said:
"We need a deep deregulation and debureaucratisation, the reduction of interest rates and the strengthening of a renewed financial system so that industrial policy can flourish".
Abascal called for Mexico's public administration to be made more efficient, saying government inefficiency threatened the country's international competitiveness.
He called for social policy to be re-examined, not to raise subsidies but to make poor Mexicans economically active and self-sufficient.
Income tax cuts and modest real wage rises could reactivate internal demand and make up in extra sales tax revenue what was lost in income tax revenues, he added.
